items.title: PCRS and NHS Wales primary care respiratory update, Cardiff, 20 October 2026
items.summary: PCRS is running a one-day essential primary care respiratory update in Cardiff on Tuesday 20 October 2026, with NHS Wales Performance and Improvement and members of the National Respiratory Audit Programme. A concentrated Welsh primary care respiratory audience.

items.title: How surgical causes can mimic reflux in infants – and how not to miss them
items.summary: Dilemmas in paediatrics: In the final part in this series, GPwER in paediatrics Dr David Capehorn looks at three surgical diagnoses that can initially resemble infant reflux, and the clinical patterns that should prompt urgent…

items.title: GP practice manager ‘knocking on patient doors’ to prevent list-cleansing removals
items.summary: Exclusive GP practice staff personally ‘knocked on doors’ of patients to ensure they were not removed from patient lists amid a national ‘list-cleansing’ drive. NHS England’s ongoing aggressive list-cleansing exercise is targeting six to seven million patients in total, Pulse has previously revealed.

items.title: Research brings Strep A vaccine ‘a step closer’, says MHRA
items.summary: New research has brought a vaccine against group A streptococcus bacterium (Strep A) a step closer to reality, the UK’s medicines watchdog has said.

items.title: Scheme to support veterans has ‘changed GP practice culture’
items.summary: A scheme which supports GP teams to improve healthcare access for veteran patients has ‘changed practice culture’, a study has suggested.

items.title: Nurses urged to ‘never give up’ on pursuing leadership roles
items.summary: A general practice nurse (GPN) has encouraged nurses to step into leadership roles to help tackle health inequalities.

items.title: Former Royal Navy nurse to honour family and fallen at Cenotaph
items.summary: The Remembrance Sunday march past the Cenotaph in Whitehall this year will feature former Royal Navy nurse Sue Warner, a veteran of the conflicts in the Falkland Islands and Afghanistan.

items.title: How this frailty team is helping older patients stay independent and avoid hospital
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: Practice nurses urged to champion veteran health scheme
items.summary: In the lead up to Remembrance Day, practice nurses are being encouraged to champion a health scheme to provide the best possible care and treatment for Armed Forces veterans.

items.title: ICBs planning to spend less on neighbourhood services following restructuring, NAO finds
items.summary: Several ICBs are expecting to spend less money on developing neighbourhood health and community services following reductions in running costs, the public spending watchdog has found.

items.title: NHS workforce plan being reassessed due to AI advances, says health secretary
items.summary: The NHS workforce plan has been delayed again because advances in AI has caused the Government to reassess staffing numbers, the health secretary has said.

items.title: Concern practice nurses ‘forgotten’ as health secretary puts focus on GPs
items.summary: Concerns have been raised that nurses working in primary care and community settings have been ‘forgotten’ amid the health secretary’s plans to shift more care into the community.

items.title: Scheme to support veterans has ‘changed GP practice culture’
items.summary: A scheme which supports general practice nurses and teams to improve healthcare access for veteran patients has ‘changed GP practice culture’, a study has suggested.

items.title: District nurses are ‘the linchpin’ of shifting care out of hospitals, minister told
items.summary: The government has once again been warned that its plans to shift care towards the community will be ‘extremely difficult’ without district nurses – a profession that must not be seen as an ‘optional extra’.

items.title: Self-referral to the GMC is classic self harm
items.summary: Copperfield attempts to get to the bottom of why GPs are needlessly referring themselves to the GMC Remember resilience? That was a thing with GPs a while back, wasn’t it? Everyone was being, or was being encouraged to be, resilient. Because that was what you needed to be to survive as a GP.

items.title: NHS England in discussions with GPs about taking over outpatient budget
items.summary: NHS England is in discussions with a group of GPs about practices ‘owning the outpatient budget’, the commissioner’s chief executive has revealed.

items.title: ICB staff cuts risk loss of essential skills, watchdog warns
items.summary: Plans to cut around a third of integrated care board (ICB) staff could leave them without the expertise to deliver long-term improvements in population health, the National Audit Office (NAO) has warned.

items.title: GPs ‘should monitor diabetes risk’ in months after starting patients on antipsychotics
items.summary: Significant metabolic changes are seen in the first 90 days of use of antipsychotic medications, say researchers who recommend closer monitoring at the start.

items.title: Last chance to register for free Pulse LIVE Liverpool event this month
items.summary: GPs have a final chance to register for Pulse LIVE Liverpool, which will cover the latest NICE diabetes guidance, ADHD management and shared care, polypharmacy and the new chickenpox vaccination programme.

items.title: MPs warn of ‘dangerous gaps’ in regulation of cosmetic treatments
items.summary: Failures to regulate cosmetic treatments such as fillers and Botox have exposed consumers to avoidable harm, MPs have warned in a report calling for urgent action to close gaps in safety standards.

items.title: ‘We’ll end up in the wrong place’ if A&G is ‘overused’, warns CMO
items.summary: The NHS will ‘end up in the wrong place’ if GP advice and guidance (A&G) is ‘overused’, England’s chief medical officer has told Pulse.

items.title: Plans to cut community nurses from children’s service dropped
items.summary: Proposals to cut community staff nurses from Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service have been revised by the county council following a public consultation. Suffolk’s Healthy Child Service currently covers health visiting, school nursing and support for young parents.

items.title: NMC officially launches four-year midwifery regulation strategy
items.summary: The Nursing and Midwifery Council (NMC) has officially launched its four-year strategy for midwifery regulation, following approval by the regulator’s governing council in September.

items.title: BMA warns GPs against ‘unnecessary’ and ‘erroneous’ GMC self-referrals
items.summary: ‘Unnecessary’ and ‘erroneous’ self-referrals to the GMC are a bigger issue than under-reporting, the BMA has said in new advice to doctors.

items.title: Five-year UK settlement path to remain open to doctors
items.summary: Public service workers including doctors and nurses will still be able to settle in the UK after five years, the Government has announced as part its new ‘earned settlement model’.

items.title: Last chance to register for Pulse LIVE Belfast
items.summary: GPs in Northern Ireland are invited to register for the free Pulse LIVE conference in Belfast next week.

items.title: Government scraps plan for 15-year settlement wait for migrant care workers
items.summary: The Home Office has announced new rules of settlement for migrant care workers following a review of its planned reforms originally set out in November 2025.

items.title: MMRV catch-up call as 15k children with chickenpox consulted by GP
items.summary: A total of 3,037 children and young people were hospitalised with chickenpox in England last year, according to new data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Nurses graduate with more debt than doctors, RCN analysis finds
items.summary: Nursing students in England are graduating with more debt than medical students despite studying for shorter degrees and earning less throughout their careers, new analysis by the Royal College of Nursing (RCN) has found.

items.title: GPs warn prescribing budget overhaul could impact patient care
items.summary: GPs have warned that plans to overhaul practice prescribing budgets across three Midlands counties could put pressure on them to cut costs at the expense of patient care.

items.title: ‘Are GPs really best placed to take on long-term management of ADHD?’
items.summary: Dr David Turner reflects on the growing pressures surrounding ADHD diagnosis and management, and why GPs cannot continue to shoulder the burden During GP training, we are taught that the bereaved fluctuate back and forth between five stages: denial, anger bargaining, depression and acceptance.

items.title: Warning over ‘decimated’ community nursing workforce
items.summary: The community nursing workforce has seen a sharp decline across district nursing, health visiting and school nursing services, but a slight increase in nurses working in general practice, according to analysis by the Nuffield Trust.

items.title: Government confirms eligibility for spring 2027 Covid vaccination
items.summary: Covid-19 vaccinations will be offered to adults aged 75 and over, immunosuppressed people aged six months and over, and residents of care homes for older adults in spring 2027, the government has confirmed.

items.title: Renewed chickenpox vaccination appeal after thousands of child hospitalisations
items.summary: A total of 3,037 children and young people were hospitalised with chickenpox in England last year, according to new data from the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA).

items.title: Domperidone prescribing guidance updated over severe hypertension risk
items.summary: A new contraindication for the dopamine receptor antagonist domperidone has been introduced by the Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA), advising that the medicine must no longer be used in patients with confirmed or suspected phaeochromocytoma due to a risk of severe hypertension.

items.title: NHSE sets out requirements for pharmacy prescribing including GP communication
items.summary: NHS England has set out requirements for pharmacies delivering prescribing services, including sending GP practices information on all prescribing activity.

items.title: Propranolol safety concerns prompt calls for NICE guideline review
items.summary: Pharmacy bodies have sent an open letter to the National Institute of Clinical Excellence (NICE) calling for a review of the clinical guideline for generalised anxiety disorder and panic disorder in adults, known as CG113, following patient safety concerns associated with propranolol.

items.title: MHRA approves new oral treatment for plaque psoriasis
items.summary: The Medicines and Healthcare products Regulatory Agency (MHRA) has approved a new oral treatment for moderate to severe plaque psoriasis in adults and adolescents aged 12 and over.

items.title: Skincare trends: how nurses can guide children and young people
items.summary: Given the physiological differences in the skin of children and young people compared to adults, elaborate multi-step skincare routines – which have become increasingly popular on social media – can risk damaging the skin barrier rather than protecting it.

items.title: NHS safety investigations body will no longer be abolished, Government confirms
items.summary: The Government is set to reverse its decision to abolish the Health Services Safety Investigations Body (HSSIB) and transfer its investigative functions to the CQC.

items.title: New CQC chief executive takes up post
items.summary: A new CQC chief executive has now taken up post, the watchdog has announced – one year after Sir Julian Hartley resigned over a care quality inquiry.

items.title: Fewer employers making ‘disproportionate’ FtP referrals of ethnic minority doctors, GMC says
items.summary: Fewer employers are referring disproportionate numbers of ethnic minority or internationally qualified doctors to fitness-to-practise tribunals, according to the GMC.

items.title: Acne: Why treatment can fail – and how to improve outcomes
items.summary: As part of our Pulse Live sessions highlights, GPwER in Dermatology Dr Bilal Khan explains why acne can fail to respond to treatment – and how to support improved outcomes Acne is an inflammatory skin disease affecting the pilosebaceous unit (hair follicle, sebaceous gland and arrector pili muscle) which has a chronic…

items.title: Myasthenia gravis: what it is, and when to suspect it
items.summary: Once in a lifetime: Continuing our series on conditions that GPs may only rarely encounter, GP Dr James Chambers considers the rare disorder myasthenia gravis Note details of the case in this article have been altered to ensure anonymity What is myasthenia gravis?

items.title: Cold weather associated with 2,200 deaths in England last year
items.summary: Cold weather was associated with 2,200 deaths in England during winter last year, a new report from the UK Health Security Agency has found. The UKHSA latest cold mortality monitoring report shows that 2,200 deaths were associated with cold weather across five cold weather episodes in 2025/26.

items.title: About 500 GP practices affected by website outage, NHS England confirms
items.summary: NHS England has confirmed that about 500 practices have been affected by disruption to their websites, after a company providing website services entered administration.

items.title: Join us for the final Nursing in Practice virtual event of the year
items.summary: After a fantastic year of virtual and face-to-face events, there’s still one more opportunity to join Nursing in Practice before the year ends. Taking place online on 3 December, Nursing in Practice Virtual: Diabetes and Respiratory rounds off our events calendar with 5.5 hours of free CPD.

items.title: Concerns raised over end of funding increase requirement for children’s mental health
items.summary: A decision to end specific ring-fenced funding increases for children and young people’s mental health services undermines the Government’s commitment to reduce waiting times in this group, a think tank has warned.

items.title: Psoriasis in primary care: ten tips for nurses
items.summary: Psoriasis is a common skin condition, thought to affect roughly 1.3–2.8% of people in the UK. However, experts suggest that both its prevalence and incidence are probably underestimated, because many people with mild psoriasis never seek advice from a healthcare professional.

items.title: UKHSA data highlights impact of flu on GP visits and missed work
items.summary: Almost one in seven people visit their GP when they have symptoms of flu, according to two years of surveillance data from the UK Health Security Agency.

items.title: More than half of GPNs still without pay rise for 2026/27
items.summary: Only four in 10 (38%) nurses working in general practice have received a pay rise for the 2026/27 financial year, according to a survey by the Royal College of Nursing (RCN).

items.title: Too many GPs still face uncertainty about employment, RCGP president warns
items.summary: The president of the RCGP has warned that ‘too many’ GPs still face uncertainty about employment and conditions, and promised to ‘fight’ for more opportunities for the profession.

items.title: RCN urges review body to address ‘continuing failures’ in GPN pay
items.summary: The independent pay review body for GPs has been urged to address a lack of annual pay uplifts for many general practice nursing staff and to make clear in its recommendations for 2027/28 that funding for nurse pay should be ‘protected’.

items.title: Pulse virtual event to feature sessions on COPD and diabetes
items.summary: GPs are invited to a free two-day virtual event in November designed to provide practical clinical updates and learning that can be applied directly in practice..

items.title: Autumn Budget: government to ‘ringfence’ spending for prevention
items.summary: The chancellor has used his first Budget to outline plans for ‘ringfenced’ spending for prevention efforts and an independent review on productivity and AI in the NHS. John Healey also reiterated plans for a National Care Service that helps ‘take the burden off’ of families and the NHS.

items.title: Budget provides extra £190m for NHS winter pressures but no mention of GPs
items.summary: The Autumn budget has provided an additional £190m to support the NHS to manage ‘additional pressures over the winter’ – but GP leaders and experts have pointed out that the chancellor has failed to address the falling share of funding for general practice.

items.title: How this nursing team is improving recruitment and retention in general practice
items.summary: We caught up with the Nurse/Nursing Team of the Year shortlist ahead of this year’s General Practice Awards, taking place on 4 December at the Novotel London West in Hammersmith.

items.title: The vanishingly small chance of hospital care
items.summary: Copperfield on how hospitals seem to be able to find endless amount of ways to avoid seeing patients This blog is not about the forthcoming consultant strikes. But I do want to highlight that, in announcing them, the BMA Consultants Committee described consultants as, ‘the most senior and skilled doctors in the NHS’.

items.title: Healthwatch to be ‘retained’ in Government U-turn
items.summary: The Government has announced that Healthwatch will no longer be scrapped, in a U-turn on its previous position. The Department of Health and Social Care said Healthwatch England and local Healthwatch organisations will now instead be ‘retained’ and ‘strengthened’.

items.title: GP practices’ websites ‘taken down’ after company enters administration
items.summary: GP practices in England and Wales are experiencing disruption to their websites, after a company providing their practices’ websites entered administration. Practices in Gloucestershire said they had been advised by NHS England at the end of last week ‘that Silicon Practice had gone into administration’.

items.title: ‘Slow and inadequate’ data on social care staff deaths during Covid crisis
items.summary: Governments have been urged to develop methods of collecting and publishing data on the deaths of adult social care workers during a pandemic.

items.title: Deprivation worsens mental health in children with intellectual disabilities, study finds
items.summary: Children and young people with intellectual developmental disabilities (IDD) from disadvantaged backgrounds are more likely to experience mental health difficulties, according to new research led by University College London (UCL).

items.title: ICB monitoring GP practices for ‘low performance’ on GP-to-patient ratios
items.summary: Exclusive One ICB has said it is monitoring nearly a fifth of its GP practices for ‘negative variation’ relating to their GP-to-patient ratios, and is considering remedial action.

items.title: ‘Early-career GPs must have a seat at the table when it comes to the future of general practice’
items.summary: New RCGP First5 co-chairs Drs Deepthi Lavu and Tom France on why supporting early-career GPs is so important for the future of general practice We are delighted to introduce ourselves as the newly elected national First5 GP representatives on the RCGP Council.

items.title: Stoptober: How nurses can help patients quit smoking
items.summary: With Stoptober raising awareness of the benefits of quitting smoking, lead nurse Marieke Strange shares practical tips for primary care nurses to support patients to stop smoking without judgement and celebrate every step towards success. It is always a good idea for patients to stop smoking.

items.title: ‘AI can diagnose, but GPs’ empathy will always be needed’
items.summary: The Doctor’s Communication Handbook has been an invaluable companion to GPs for over 30 years.

items.title: LMCs to debate calling for LES funding to be moved into core
items.summary: LMC leaders are set to debate calling for future national GP contracts to incorporate existing local enhanced services (LESs), with recurrent funding attached.

items.title: QICN sets out key asks for community nursing ahead of Autumn Budget
items.summary: The Queen’s Institute of Community Nursing (QICN) has urged the chancellor to use Wednesday’s Autumn Budget to ensure money reaches the community nursing services expected to support the shift away from hospitals.

items.title: GP leaders to vote on pushing for ‘unequivocal contractual right’ to refer
items.summary: England’s GP leaders will vote on opposing mandatory single point of access and pushing for an ‘unequivocal contractual right’ to refer a patient directly for specialist assessment.

items.title: Tributes paid to nurse killed in attack during Ebola response
items.summary: A nurse has been killed after being attacked while responding to an Ebola alert in a rural town in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). A health worker has also been left ‘severely injured’ and in hospital, according to the World Health Organization (WHO).

items.title: Empowering people through diet and lifestyle in type 2 diabetes management
items.summary: Dietary change, physical activity, weight management and self-management education are fundamental components of type 2 diabetes care.

items.title: Persistent pruritus: what primary care nurses need to know
items.summary: Chronic pruritus is common in primary care and can significantly affect sleep, wellbeing and quality of life, particularly in older adults. Persistent itch may result from dermatological disease, medication, dry skin or underlying systemic illness.

items.title: Supporting people with Parkinson's in primary care
items.summary: Parkinson's is a multi-system condition, and although patients will generally be under the care of a specialist team, they will often present to primary care before and after diagnosis.

items.title: Holistic support of patients with breast cancer in primary care
items.summary: The impact of breast cancer is multi-faceted and can extend far beyond the period of active cancer treatment, affecting the person physically, psychologically, socially, economically and spiritually.

items.title: A guide to common childhood illnesses: chickenpox
items.summary: Chickenpox (varicella) is a highly infectious viral disease that is usually self-limiting in children but can cause serious complications in adults and vulnerable groups.

items.title: Turning a few minutes into an opportunity
items.summary: Practice Nursing, Volume 37, Issue 11, Page 405-405, November 2026.

items.title: Hospital consultants to strike following lack of formal negotiations with Government
items.summary: Hospital consultants in England are planning to strike next month following a lack of formal negotiations with the Government, the BMA has announced. The strike action is planned to take place between 06:59am on 25 November and 06:59am on 27 November, with formal notices to follow, the union said.

items.title: Blood clot prevention medicine recalled over formulation error
items.summary: A medication that helps prevent blood clots and reduces the risk of heart attacks and strokes has been recalled due to a formulation error.

items.title: BMA advises GPs to raise formal dispute with health boards over IT provision
items.summary: GPs in Scotland have been advised by the BMA to raise a formal dispute with their health board over disruption to IT provision, which has caused ‘considerable anxiety’ and admin delays for practices.

items.title: Concern over GP practice buildings as NHS maintenance backlog revealed
items.summary: GP practices and care homes will be impacted by flooding and burst pipes in winter without investment into NHS buildings, The King’s Fund has warned.

items.title: ‘Why GPs must look for their “missing” patients’
items.summary: Professor Andrea Williamson explains how understanding missingness in healthcare can help GPs tackle health inequalities and reconnect patients with the care they need The attention of most GPs most of the time is on the patients who attend the practice, make the phone calls, and request input; those who are able to…

items.title: DHSC confirms first areas to roll out domestic abuse support via GP practices
items.summary: The Department of Health and Social Care has confirmed the 12 ICB areas in which GP practices will have access to independent domestic abuse and sexual violence (DASV) specialist workers funded through a new programme.

items.title: Interim advisor for social care nursing appointed at NHSE
items.summary: A mental health nurse of 40 years has been seconded to NHS England’s chief nursing officer (CNO) team to work as a senior advisor for adult social care nursing.

items.title: Government neighbourhood ambitions risk failing amid lack of GP investment, RCGP warns
items.summary: The Government’s ambitions around neighbourhood health risk failing without greater investment into general practice, the RCGP has warned.

items.title: Paediatric lung assessments: tips for practice nurses
items.summary: At a recent Nursing in Practice virtual event, consultant nurse and doctoral researcher specialising in respiratory medicine, Aleksandra Gawlik-Lipinski, offered advice and guidance on paediatric lung assessments.

items.title: Blood test may help sepsis patients come off antibiotics sooner
items.summary: A daily blood test could help critically ill patients with sepsis to come off antibiotics sooner, a new study suggests. The ADAPT-Sepsis study examined how clinicians responded to automated advice generated from daily blood tests designed to guide decisions on when antibiotic treatment could safely end.

items.title: Greater national oversight needed for obesity treatment, urges parliamentary committee
items.summary: Services to treat obesity should be ‘overhauled and reimagined’, a cross-party parliamentary committee has said. The Health and Social Care Committee is urging the government to reframe obesity as a ‘chronic, relapsing condition with life-long physiological impacts’ and adapt how patients receive treatment.

items.title: GP contract negotiations for 2027/28 to start next month, says BMA
items.summary: GP contract negotiations for the next financial year are due to start in November, the BMA’s GP committee has confirmed. In an update to LMCs, the GPC said that contract negotiations for 2027/28 are now due to start next month, after ‘further discussion’ with NHS England.

items.title: What does the Fonagy review into ADHD mean for GPs?
items.summary: Pulse takes an in-depth look at the recent independent review into ADHD and autism ‘Mental health conditions, ADHD and autism overlap in many people’s lives, but they differ in important ways: in how they arise, how they develop, how they affect day-to-day life, and how they are best understood and supported,’ says…

items.title: Five AI tools approved for identifying prostate cancer on MRI scans
items.summary: Five artificial intelligence tools for more accurately detecting prostate cancer in MRI scans have been approved for use on the NHS. NICE said the tools have the potential to act like a ‘second pair of eyes’, helping radiologists review prostate MRI scans and improve accuracy and consistency of diagnosis.

items.title: Joint GP and community pharmacy conference to return for 2027 in London
items.summary: GPs and community pharmacy professionals are invited to a free-to-attend conference in London next June which aims to bring the two groups together to collaborate as the Government aims to shift care out of hospital.

items.title: NHS 111 calls reduced following GP online access changes, CQC finds
items.summary: Calls to NHS 111 have been decreasing following GP online access changes and the launch of Pharmacy First, the CQC has said in its annual assessment of health and social care in England.

items.title: CQC flags ‘considerable’ regional variation in practice nurse workforce
items.summary: A shortage of practice nurses in some areas is increasing pressures for existing staff and reducing capacity to provide timely care, the healthcare watchdog has warned.

items.title: Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference returns in 2027
items.summary: Primary care nursing professionals will have the opportunity to explore how closer working between general practice and community pharmacy can improve patient care at the second annual Community Pharmacy and General Practice Conference, which moves to London in 2027.

items.title: Falling immigration could put pressure on NHS finances, analysis warns
items.summary: The NHS has become increasingly reliant on revenue from the Immigration Health Surcharge (HIS) which generated almost £2.5bn in 2024/25, according to the Nuffield Trust.

items.title: MPs demand weight management overhaul amid ‘unambitious’ Mounjaro rollout
items.summary: NHS weight management care needs to be completely overhauled, say MPs who found poor access to a range of treatments, including drugs and surgery. The Health and Social Care Committee said obesity should be treated as a long-term, managed condition like diabetes.

items.title: Alzheimer’s trial launches to test diabetes and ADHD drugs
items.summary: A large UK study has been launched to test several drugs for Alzheimer’s disease that are already being used for other conditions. The multi-arm adaptive randomised controlled trial being run across 30 NHS sites when fully operational will initially test metformin and atomoxetine with results expected by 2030.

items.title: Clinical casebook: Common nail conditions
items.summary: In our latest CPD module, GPwER in dermatology Dr Chitra Nair discusses four cases involving common nail conditions and advises on their appropriate diagnosis and management. Complete the full module today and earn 2 CPD points.

items.title: Syncope as a clue to sarcoidosis
items.summary: Under the radar: GPSI in respiratory medicine Dr Andrew Powell describes how an episode of syncope led to a diagnosis of sarcoidosis, and the clues that can help GPs recognise this multisystem condition Note: details of the case in this article have been altered to ensure anonymity The case A 55-year-old woman…

items.title: Record 5,000 doctors secure GP training places as competition eases
items.summary: A record number of resident doctors secured GP training posts this year, the Government has announced.
